issues.what: Opening full-disk Earth (0.0-2.07 s) is effectively a still image: mean pixel change over 2 s is 0.25/255, no visible turning, while the script shot says 'turning slowly'. It is the hook shot and the loop target. No single frozen run is over 1 s by ffmpeg freezedetect (the picture changes by tiny steps at ~0.6 s and ~1.5 s), so this is not a BLOCK, but the first 2 s read as a freeze-frame.
issues.fix: Re-render with a different source_start in the DSCOVR EPIC film where the planet visibly rotates, or interpolate frames; keep the last shot on the same span so the loop still matches.

issues.what: From 23.1 s to the end the EPIC Earth shots advance as ~1 fps stop-motion: new picture every 0.97 s (23.1, 24.07, 25.03, 26.0, 28.1, 29.07), with a large jump in longitude at each step (Asia at 23.0, Arabia at 24.0, Africa at 25.0), and near-still between steps (26.07-27.9 changes only 0.23/255 over 1.8 s). It reads as a slideshow, not a turning planet, for the last 7 s. Each hold is under 1 s so it does not meet the frozen-over-1-s block rule.
issues.fix: Swap the span for a smoother EPIC segment or apply motion interpolation (minterpolate or blend) to the three EPIC shots in the render; the narration and captions need no change.

issues.what: captions.json: the Instagram caption has no AI-voice disclosure. YouTube ('Narration made with an AI voice.') and the Twitter text ('Made with AI.') have it.
issues.fix: Add 'Narration made with an AI voice.' to the Instagram caption (or confirm the platform AI label is switched on when scheduling).

issues.what: Hook title ('THROWN EAST AT 1,000 MPH', 0-2.6 s) fades out by 2.6 s and the '1,000 MPH AT THE EQUATOR' label appears at 2.7 s in the same screen position, so they never overlap. Label stays to about 5.4 s. Both are readable, over the safe zone (about 22% of frame height) and 40% above the captions (captions at about 65%). Dark vertical stripe inside the label box after '1,000' (and after each '1' in '1 DAY = 1 YEAR') is a highlight-box rendering artifact, cosmetic only.
issues.fix: None required; optionally flatten the box layer in the assembler.

issues.what: '1 DAY = 1 YEAR' label shows from 14.8 s to about 17.1 s, matching 'one day lasts a whole year' (15.46-17.04 s). It is readable and clear of the captions and the hook title.

A small dark round spot sits fixed in the frame at about (55%, 17%) through 2.1-5.0 s while the ground moves past: a lens or sensor dust spot in the NASA film, not an object. Could be read as an artifact.

'The oceans drain toward the poles' (21.08-22.78 s) is shown over green airglow or aurora at the night horizon; the picture is real but does not illustrate the claim. Also 19.1-21.0 s (night, city lights) and 21-22.9 s are dark with a black lower half; none is a black or frozen stretch over 1 s.
issues.fix: Optional: use a daylit polar or ocean span for that line.

issues.what: Phrase onsets after the cut pauses are hard: level jumps from about -30 dB to -12 dB within 20 ms (e.g. 'Everything' 6.66, 'After' 14.72, 'Luckily' 25.84, 'The' 21.12, 'At' 2.08), and 'What' starts at sample 0 at -18 dB. faster-whisper recovered every word, so none is dropped, but a leading consonant or breath may be trimmed. I could not listen to the audio; this is from level analysis only. Speech rate is about 150 wpm (73 words in 29.2 s), within natural range.
issues.fix: Have a person listen once at 00:00, 00:07 and 00:26 for clipped onsets; if audible, add a 30-40 ms pad or fade-in at the pause cuts.

issues.what: Facts: '1,000 mph at the equator' matches the 1,040.6 mph source (Wikipedia, 'about a thousand' is fair rounding); six months of day and night and 'everything not attached keeps going' match space.com; oceans migrating to the poles and an equatorial continent match the Esri/Fraczek source. 'Air faster than any hurricane' (12.0-14.4 s) and 'no known force could do it' (25.9-28.0 s) are not stated in the three listed sources, though both are physically sound (about 1,000 mph versus a roughly 160-190 mph hurricane).
issues.fix: Optional: add a source for those two lines to script.json sources.

issues.what: Checks passed: no NASA logo, watermark, astronaut face or baked-in text in any of the 60 frames (ISS solar-array edge at the left, 17.0-18.5 s, and sun lens flares are real hardware and optics); every scene change coincides with a scripted shot boundary (cuts detected at 2.07, 5.43, 6.63, 9.2, 11.67, 14.73, 17.2, 19.13, 22.87 s plus EPIC stepping), no shot jumps scene mid-shot; no impossible physics (all real film); no talking person; no silence (music bed under the voice, lowest 10 ms level above -45 dB); longest single shot about 3.8 s; first frame shows the Earth with the title; first words 'What if Earth stopped spinning' carry the stake; final shot returns to the opening Americas-facing Earth, so the loop works and 'Still, people ask:' runs into 'What if Earth stopped spinning right now?'.
